description: The plot illustrates how “Reliability Score” varies with “Cost” for three different approaches (a 3-model ensemble, a 2-model ensemble, and a single model) shown as three colored lines. The x-axis is labeled “Cost,” appears to use a linear scale, and shows tick labels at 2-unit intervals (2, 4, 6, 8), spanning roughly from 0 to about 10 (units not shown). The y-axis is labeled “Reliability Score,” appears linear, and shows labeled ticks at 30, 50, and 70, spanning roughly from 30 up to around 90. The blue line (3-Model Ensemble) is a solid line with circular markers and increases across the cost range, starting near the low-80s at the leftmost point, passing through the mid-to-high 80s around cost 4, and ending near about 90 at the highest cost. The red line (2-Model Ensemble) is a solid line with circular markers and also increases, starting slightly above the blue line near the low-to-mid 80s at the leftmost point, reaching the high 80s around cost 4, and ending just below the blue line near the high 80s to about 90 at the highest cost. The yellow line (single-model line) is a solid line with circular markers and decreases as cost increases, starting near about 90 at the leftmost point, dropping to around the mid-70s near cost 4, and continuing downward toward the right edge of the plot (the final point is not fully visible in the provided image).
